correctness.rationale: A matching is maximal iff its unmatched vertices span no edge. In a complete multipartite graph this is equivalent to the unmatched set lying in one part. Choosing that set leaves a residual complete multipartite graph that must be perfectly matched, giving the enumerator without double counting; the empty unmatched set is handled separately. The stated perfect-matching finite sum follows by edge-type counts, and the size spectrum follows from the exact largest-part criterion for a multipartite perfect matching. Exhaustive direct graph enumeration through order eight agrees coefficient-by-coefficient.

originality.rationale: Searches under average maximal matching, maximal-matching polynomial/enumerator, complete multipartite, residual perfect matching, and equimatchable aliases did not locate an equivalent distribution formula. Zhang's recent full text treats bicyclic core classes and has no multipartite/complete/bipartite occurrence. Chen--Lian treats all ordinary matchings in complete multipartite graphs for matching energy, which does not state or imply which of them are maximal. The closest database result is an extremal lower bound by cyclomatic number, not an exact distribution for a given multipartite graph.
residual_risks: The 2023 Engbers--Erey article was not lawfully available in full text during the run, so a special complete-multipartite formula hidden there cannot be ruled out solely from accessible metadata.

value.rationale: The result gives the entire maximal-matching size distribution for a canonical dense graph class, with the current average-size statistic as an immediate first moment. The structural reduction is nontrivial and reusable: maximality becomes a one-part unmatched-set condition, and every coefficient becomes a residual perfect-matching count. It therefore supplies exact finite data beyond a single optimum or isolated example and directly complements current work on average sizes of maximal matchings.
